sheet_or_frame: Sheet G1-C: Aurennais fauna, 15 species and five habitats
ideas_to_keep: Fifteen warm-country animals. Duneskimmer (deserts and dunes, common; gazelle with wide hooves for sand, goes days without water). Sunspire Lynx (rocky hills, rare; caracal-like with long ears and a heat-shedding crest). Terrace Ram (cliffs and highlands; huge spiral horns, fights on terraced cliffs and ruins). Saltspine Monitor (coasts and islands, uncommon; aggressive lizard whose spines excrete salt crust: a hostile). Oasis Hare (deserts and oases; big ears). Scarlet Ibis (coastal wetlands, common; sign of healthy marsh). Dunescorpion (deserts, uncommon; venom causes paralysis and fever, hunts at night: overlaps the existing Sand Scorpion). Mirage Fox (fennec-like, scavenges ruins and caravan routes). Cliffswift (coasts and sea stacks, common; swirling flocks). Amber Shellcrab (tide pools, common; shells prized for local crafts and trade: a harvestable). Cypress Stalker (rivers and marshes, rare; violet heron whose plumage shifts with the light). Sand Wyrm (dunes, rare; massive burrowing predator, rarely seen, known by its tracks and sand funnels: a set-piece hostile). Glasswing Moth (oases and ruins; crystalline wings drawn to moonlight and flowering plants, "resonate with ambient magic": a night ingredient). Sunbeak Vulture (deserts and cliffs, common; carrion cleaner). Spined Gekko (ruins, rare; nocturnal, climbs walls). Habitats: turquoise coastal shores, salt marshes and lagoons with flamingos, olive groves and terraced farmland, deserts and dunes with rock arches, cliffs and islets.
notes: Fills the fauna gap for Aurenne and fits Michael's Mediterranean / North African reading (olive groves, dunes, salt marsh, terraces). The Sand Wyrm is the island's big strange beast; Dunescorpion would reskin the Sand Scorpion. Names are proposals.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet G1-B: the Markish fauna, 15 species and five habitats
ideas_to_keep: Fifteen cold-country animals. Icehorn (alpine peaks, uncommon; shaggy mountain goat with huge curled hollow horns that moan in the wind, a sound idea). Frostreach Bear (mountain forests, rare; pale, larger than southern bears, hunts in packs in hard winters: a hostile). Stormlynx (high ridges; snowshoe paws, long ear tufts). Ironpine Elk (forests and valleys, common; dark, sweeping antlers). Skyraven (cliffs and peaks, common; follows travellers and scavenges battlefields). Stonefang Wolf (mountain forests, common; bigger than lowland wolves, packs in winter: a variant of the Snow Wolf). Craghorn Ram (high cliffs; scales near-vertical rock). Glacial Marmot (alpine slopes, common; hibernates). Stormshrike (tundra, uncommon; white falcon that stoops and hangs in the wind). Snowleap Hare (tundra and forests, common; coat changes with the season). Frostspine Lizard (rocky slopes, rare; mineral-hardened scales that store sunlight). Riverjaw Salmon (rivers, common; leaps the falls on its migration: fishing and a set piece). Tundra Grouse (highlands; flushes noisily from the snow). Icecrab (northern coasts, uncommon; armoured crab "harvested for their meat", dangerous when cornered). Shatterback (coastal waters, rare; a colossal slow armoured sea beast whose back is mistaken for rocks by sailors: a sea landmark or encounter). Habitats: high peaks, snow forests, rivers and lakes with waterfalls, tundra, northern coasts with sea stacks.
notes: Fills the fauna gap for the Mark. Stonefang Wolf and Frostreach Bear overlap the existing Snow Wolf and Cave Bear and could reskin them. Shatterback is the one strange beast: a candidate for the sea (the game has sharks and whales only). Names are proposals.

sheet_or_frame: Key frame 5 variant: the gate in the hillside, wider
ideas_to_keep: Wider framing of the concentric-ring gate; reads well at distance.
notes: Variant of OG-037.

sheet_or_frame: Board 12: the Mark, settlements and life (first pass)
ideas_to_keep: Settlement kinds: mountain village, cliff village, lakeside settlement, pass hamlet, mining camp, watchtower. Details: turf roofs, stone-and-timber, carved animal gables, big stone chimneys, palisades, standing stones, clan banners. Fjord harbour, shipyard, lighthouse, whaling station, dry docks. Longhouse hall, home and tavern interiors. Materials: furs, wool, bone and antler, glass and crystal.
notes: Superseded by OG-034. Politics conflict: a "Highhouse" and "Council of Houses" ruling from a capital; canon has the Captains' League, no capital.

sheet_or_frame: Board 12: the Mark, settlements and life (refined)
ideas_to_keep: Cliff city on terraces linked by stone bridges and rope walkways; fjord port; mining town with lifts and tunnels; fortress town on a pass; remote settlement under the aurora (whaling, fishing). Settlement kinds as OG-033 plus coastal outpost. Mark style: carved gables and roof finials, stone-and-timber, snow-shedding steep roofs, runic knotwork, banners by house and clan, palisade gates, cliff walkways. Daily life: winter markets, communal feasts, shipbuilding, guided mountain travel. Materials: local stone, timber, iron, furs and wool, bone and antler, crystal.
notes: Names (Skardrun, Fjordhold, Ironreach, Stonewatch, Glassfjord) are proposals. "Highhold / Council of Houses / capital" conflicts with the Captains' League. The look fits the canon: timber halls, dark shingle, palisades, squat stone garrisons.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet H4: survival, crafting and rural life: resources, crops, animal products, water, tools, stations, outputs
ideas_to_keep: The fullest resource list, by island. Adds to H3: river stone, silver and saltpeter (gunpowder, late) in the Gatelands; schist, obsidian, glacial ice and Star Metal (very rare, from high peaks) in the Mark; red stone (pigment), obsidian and desert glass in Aurenne. Crops by island: Gatelands wheat, barley, turnip, cabbage, carrot, apple (cider), herbs; the Mark rye, potato, leek, cabbage, onion, coldroot; Aurenne olive, grape, fig, citrus, chickpea, date, lavender, spice herbs. Animal products: meat, fish, eggs, milk, honey, wool, leather, bone. Water: waterskin (4 drinks, reusable), ceramic flask (2), glass bottle (1, for potions), water barrel (ships and homes); collect from rivers, lakes, wells and rain; purify at campfires or with filters; rain catcher. Preserved foods: flour, dried meat, hardtack, cheese, dried fish, spices, pickles, smoked goods. Tools: woodcutter's axe (higher skill fells larger trees), pickaxe in tiers, gathering knife, shovel (buried finds), fishing rod (better rods reach deeper water), sickle, net. Stations: campfire, drying rack, tanning rack, grindstone, smelter, kiln, workbench, alchemy table. Outputs: planks, ingots, bricks, pottery, glass vials, ropes, cloth, arrows, tools, armour, weapons, furniture, ship parts, trade goods.
notes: Supersedes OG-015 for the resource and crop lists; OG-023 (H5) carries the cooking and camp side. Matches the planned survival scope (moderate survival, cooking, water collection, reusable containers). Saltpeter "gunpowder (late)" implies firearms, which the canon has not admitted: flag before anyone builds on it. Star Metal is a rare-material candidate with no canon yet. Livestock (cows, sheep, goats, chickens, bees) is implied and absent from the game.

sheet_or_frame: Reference: screenshot of the game's character creator today
ideas_to_keep: Nothing new to take: it records the build as it is. Four peoples (Gatelander, Markman, Aurennais, Old Blood) with one line each; look options (skin, hair colour, 21 hair styles, 16 beards, tunic, breeches, boots); the low-poly person on the left; four starting weapons with damage and a line each (sword, club, dagger, staff).
notes: A reference capture of the current UI, not concept art; keep it as the 'before' baseline for the character and UI boards. No canon conflict.

sheet_or_frame: Key frame 5 board: the old gate, with four design variations
ideas_to_keep: Gate design: concentric stone rings emerging from the hillside and disappearing underground; a narrow, dark slit entrance ("not a door, a passage"); simple repeated Weaver sigils lit amber ("amber light, not magic"); weathered, lichened stone "built for a purpose, not for beauty"; a small encampment at the foot. Four variations: V1 concentric rings, V2 offset rings, V3 broken circle (partly collapsed), V4 single spine. Notes: simple repeatable geometry for procedural generation; the player small against it; subtle amber light, not bright effects.
notes: The board names the scene "The Buried Crown"; not canon. V3 could be a failing gate, V1 a steady one.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet: the four peoples, Gatelanders page (first pass)
ideas_to_keep: Crown guards in crimson and gold: a red tabard and short cape over brown leather, embroidered with a gold sprig, worn by a man and a woman. A 'Crown authority' panel: the Crown's red and gold worn as a mark of service, over Gatelander dress rather than instead of it. Villagers with red neckerchiefs, a tradesman in a flat cap and leather apron, a woman in a headscarf and green apron dress with a basket. Gold scroll embroidery on red cloth. Palette: crimson, ochre, sage, navy, brown, cream. A market street with stalls and red banners below a castle.
notes: Earlier pass of OG-048. Captions still use the generator's 'frontier' framing ('hardened by frontier life', 'the frontier is opportunity'); the canon Gatelands is a settled home island. Its Crown colours match the canon (crimson and gold, §1.5), unlike OG-010.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet H1: botanical atlas, 16 plants per island with effects and habitats
ideas_to_keep: A look for every herb the game already has, placed by island, with effects that match HERB_DEF (Firemoss +15 health and +10% melee, Silverleaf +30 stamina and faster sprint, Heartroot +60 mana and +10% spell damage). Gatelands: Firemoss (orange-red moss on rock, moor and wastes), Deepmoss, Silverleaf, Briarweed (purple thistle-flower), Graywort, Veilwort (white bell-flowers near houses), Duilleog Ghorm (blue flowers, coast and fen, spells last longer), Goldenrod (roadsides), Thornberry, Caorthann (rowan berries, autumn woods), Caor Dubh (black berries; -10 health, +40% damage, risky), Heartroot, Fearnóg (orange cap mushrooms), Shadowcap (purple mushrooms), Mist Fern, Luibh Uisce (white water-flowers that fully restore mana). The Mark, mostly new: Coldmoss (blue, tundra), Icebloom (cold resistance), Stonecress, Frostcap (violet mushroom, frost resist), Ironleaf (red, +8 defence), Gnarlroot (cliffs; reveals hidden resources on the map), Snowthyme, Stormthistle (blue globe thistle, lightning resist), Glacier Lily (slows time briefly in combat), Rimeberry (cold resist), Shardmoss (crystal moss on cave walls, improves ore yield), Wolfsbane (high forests, rare; -40% beast damage), Pine Resin (amber on bark, for alchemy, arrows and torches), Red Clay / Cré Dearg (riverbeds; regeneration), Lichenbloom (high ruins; detects nearby gates), Skykelp (cold coastal water; longer breath). Aurenne, all new except the sea herbs: Sandlotus (heat resistance), Amberbloom (+15% fire damage), Sagepalm (reduces heat build-up), Sunpetal (+10% crafting quality), Saltthorn (salt flats; poison resist), Drakesage (strengthens poisons), Miragebloom (detects water sources), Spicethorn (chilli; improves food effects), Datefruit, Cyprus Blossom (+20% alchemy potency), Desert Truffle (underground), Jade Aloe (bleeding resist, regeneration), Sunfungus (canyons; day vision), Pearlweed, Sea Lily, Kelp. Each island closes on a habitat strip.
notes: The atlas the herb system can follow island by island; it was drawn from the game's own herb list, which is why the existing effects match. It places Wolf's Bane (unplaced in the game) in the Mark and the three sea herbs in Aurenne; Cré Dearg moves to the Mark as red clay. Leaves out Ashwort, Muirfhear and Ferrous Weed. Heartroot is drawn violet with a red heart, the game's is amber. New plants and every new effect (time slowing, gate detection, crafting quality, heat build-up) are proposals; heat and cold resistance imply a temperature rule the game does not have. Aurenne's numbering repeats 12. Companion to OG-026 (rare specimens).

sheet_or_frame: Sheet G1-D: signature species, five strange beasts per island
ideas_to_keep: The Morrowind-style strange wildlife, five per island, none of it gate-made. Gatelands: Crownstag (forest monarch, rare; antlers that grow like living branches hung with moss and epiphytes; peaceful, a landmark animal); Mossback (woodlands, uncommon; ancient slow tortoise carrying a living garden of ferns and flowers on its shell, peaceful); Bellthroat (rivers and wetlands; red frog with a huge violet throat sac whose call echoes across valleys at dusk, an ambient sound); Lanternfox (forests, rare; black fox whose fur glows blue and silver at night, used for signalling); Thornrunner (hills and farmland; long-legged quilled omnivore, very fast). The Mark: Shatterhorn (alpine peaks, rare; colossal six-legged shaggy grazer with layered crystalline horns, peaceful giant); Frostmane (snow forests; long-necked maned browser in small herds, llama-like, a candidate pack beast); Glasswing (cliffs and ridges, rare; gliding predator with translucent wings, soars between peaks); Stonejaw (tundra; armoured burrower with a shovel skull that digs through snow and rock for roots); Stormplume (open slopes, rare; towering flightless bird with layered feathers, kicks hard, territorial: a hostile). Aurenne: Redcrest (scrub and cliffs, rare; feathered raptor-like predator that hunts in packs: a hostile); Sunfan (plains and oases, rare; long-legged bird with a radiant fan crest it displays, "a symbol of beauty in Aurenne"); Mineprowler (deserts, uncommon; lithe six-legged spiny sand predator with a curled tail and webbed feet: hostile); Sailshell (deserts and dry valleys; huge tortoise with a sail-like heat-shedding shell, migrates between oases, peaceful).
notes: The best answer to §10a "strange, not stock" for the open world: wonder without menace, mostly peaceful, which the decision of 12 Oct asks for. The Mineprowler's text sits beside an unlabelled blue-and-gold coastal lizard; the six-legged scorpion-tailed beast above it is the one the text describes. Six-legged animals are a design call: are they ordinary in this world, or seams of the binding? Worth raising as a decision. Names are proposals and candidates to fill the fauna gap.

sheet_or_frame: Bestiary: classic monsters (skeleton, goblin, cave troll, slime, giant spider)
ideas_to_keep: Five dungeon foes with turnarounds, detail crops and a scene each. Skeleton: a notched sword and a round wooden shield, rags at the hips. Goblin: crouched, long ears, a long spear and a round hide shield, a scrap-leather harness. Cave troll: hunched and huge, its hide grey like stone with moss and lichen growing on it, scraps of armour lashed on, a wide fanged mouth. Slime: translucent pale green, arched like a wave, with holes through it and bones and rubble suspended inside. Giant spider: a pale, bulbous abdomen, thorny dark legs, a cluster of red eyes, egg sacs and thick webbing in a ruined hall.
notes: The dark tone is right here: these belong in the gates (decision 1). All five are in §9a: skeleton (Solas, Uisce), cave troll (Tine, Uisce, Cloch), slime (Uisce, and a magma one for Tine); the troll's mossy stone hide suits a Cloch gate. Goblins are not a kind of gate but an occupied state (§9a), so the goblin belongs to a warren in a spent gate. Filed under characters, but it is creature work; check against the creatures folder's bestiary passes.

sheet_or_frame: NPC sheet E5: five powers (leaders of the peoples)
ideas_to_keep: Costume and props for high-status figures. A Gatelander chieftain: grey-bearded, a crimson cloak over a fur collar, a gold round brooch, a sword. A sea captain of the Mark: a woman with dark red curls, a navy coat with a fur collar, a spyglass and charts. An Aurennais magistrate: a dark-haired woman with a gold circlet, an ivory gown with purple and gold trim, a scroll, a domed city behind. An Old Blood elder: grey skin, long white hair, a tall carved staff, bone and stone charms. A foreign governor: a velvet coat with fur, a ledger and a white cat. Each has a turnaround, a still life of their things, and a scene.
notes: Politics against the canon (decision 3: the canon wins): Ashenmoor is a village with Elders, not the seat of a 'High Chieftain of the Gatelanders' (the Crown rules from Coeur de Vie); the Mark has no 'Lord Admiral', only the Captains' League; Aurenne is ruled by the Compact under the Church, not a magistrate; the 'Keepers' who 'tend the Gates' contradict the Withdrawal's ban on reading (§3.1); 'Lord Esteban, Governor of the Far Shores' speaks for 'distant mainland powers' that the canon does not have. The banners (a red beast for the Gatelands, a blue wave for the Mark, purple for Aurenne) do not match the canon colours (§1.5). Names are proposals; Sorcha Ní Bhriain would suit a Gatelander, not a Markman.

sheet_or_frame: Board 14: important buildings and interiors, by island
ideas_to_keep: Exterior and interior for each nation of: tavern/inn (Aurenne a courtyard caravanserai), blacksmith, alchemy shop, guildhall, temple/shrine, library/academy, homes. Gatelands thatch and stone; the Mark timber halls with carved posts; Aurenne arcades, tilework and courtyards.
notes: A direct reference for nation-specific interior kits. "Sunhand order" is invented; the canon's church is the Church of the Weaver.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet: the four peoples, Aurennais page
ideas_to_keep: Olive to dark brown skin, curly, wavy and braided hair, headwraps and turbans: the mixed, darker-skinned people of decision 4. Light layered clothes: loose cream shirts, indigo and madder-red sashes and skirts, saffron and blue scarves, printed cotton, leather sandals and soft boots. Silver, brass and glass jewellery (coin pendants, hoops, layered necklaces). Fishermen, merchants and sailors as pairs. Guards in a red cloak over a scale cuirass with a round bronze shield and a spear. A white hillside city of domes and towers above a harbour of lateen-sailed boats; a quayside market under striped awnings. Palette: madder red, rust, saffron, indigo, sea blue, olive, sand.
notes: Fits decision 4 and §1.3 (warm, coastal, trading). The guards are captioned 'Crown guard'; the Crown is the Gatelands' alone (§1.1), and Compact guards should wear blue-and-white (§1.5). The look leans Moorish and Levantine; the Roman, Egyptian and Greek parts of decision 4 are light (the bronze tier of OG-019 could supply them). The text says 'deserts to the south' and 'eastern and western shores', a wider world than the canon's three islands.

sheet_or_frame: Combat key frame: sword and spell against a skeleton (pass with crossed blades)
ideas_to_keep: Blades crossed high in a bind, both fighters leaning in: the posture contest. The player holds a charging blue spell low behind him in the off hand, cocked to release. A dark cloak with a gold tree. A tunnel of arches lit by amber script recedes behind.
notes: Pass of OG-011, darker. The crossed-blade bind is the clearest read of a parry-then-push of the four passes; worth keeping as a pose reference for the posture system. Near duplicate of OG-063.

sheet_or_frame: Board 15: ports, roads & infrastructure (refined)
ideas_to_keep: Infrastructure set: stone roads and bridges, caravan trade routes, farms and windmills, shipyards and dry docks, lighthouses and beacons, canals, port cities, market towns, caravanserai, watchtowers and forts, toll gates, mines and quarries, aqueduct, river port and ferry. Beasts of burden: horse, mule, donkey, ox, cow, llama, camel, reindeer, highland yak, giant goat. Vehicles: covered wagon, merchant wagon, stagecoach, royal carriage, supply cart.
notes: Mines and quarries tie to the planned survival skills. Capital names are proposals.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet G1: wildlife of the three islands (first pass, 15 species mixed)
ideas_to_keep: Species not on the later sheets: Saltskim Seal (Aurennais coast, common; spotted seal near fishing villages, folklore says it sees weather coming); Embersong Thrush (Old Blood woodlands; red-breasted songbird with a fluting song at dawn and dusk that "sings differently near gate sites", a sound cue near a gate); Tidecrab (Aurennais coast; crabs prized for meat, shells used in crafts, a vivid blue kind unique to Aurenne); Stormlight Moth (forests and ruins, uncommon; iridescent night moth found near old stonework and latent magic, "said to herald change"); Warden Wolf (high forests, uncommon; larger, cleverer wolves in small disciplined packs; Markish clans claim descent from them, a lore hook); Sunshell Tortoise (southern valleys; kept in monastery gardens, shells patterned, bringers of patience); Dusk Hare (all islands; huge ears, "faint magical echoes"). Also Island Stag, Stone Goat, Gatefen Boar (said to avoid gate-touched ruins: animals that shun a gate are a readable sign), Cliffhawk (used by messengers), Marsh Heron, Redspine Fox (a good omen in some villages), River Otter, Stonecrawler Lizard (scales used in alchemy).
notes: Earlier pass of the island sheets OG-009, OG-031, OG-030 and the overview OG-084, which supersede it; keep for the species above. "Old Blood woodlands" makes the Old Blood a place, which they are not in canon (they are a people living inside each nation). Its "warmer southern lands" for the Aurennais coast contradicts the map: Aurenne is north-east and warm by island, not latitude (§1.5).

sheet_or_frame: Sheet: the four peoples, Gatelanders page
ideas_to_keep: Shorter, wiry Gatelanders with freckles and red hair common, darker hair too. Hooded wool cloaks in moss green and madder red pinned at the throat with a round brooch ('pinned collars, a hallmark of Gatelander dress'). A farmer with a pitchfork, a farm woman with an apron and a basket, a tradesman in a flat cap and apron, a woman in a patterned headscarf. Crown guards in a crimson cape and tabard with gold embroidery and a kettle helm. Layered linen sleeves, boot wraps, woven baskets, red embroidered borders. A castle above a harbour town, a tavern interior. Palette: madder red, ochre, moss, sea blue, sand, slate.
notes: The best of the three Gatelander passes (supersedes OG-038 and OG-010). It matches the canon: 'middling height, wiry, freckled, dark or red hair' (§2), the Crown's crimson and gold (§1.5), and its own line that 'Crown authority exists, but is layered over older local identity' (§1.1). The towns are drawn half-timbered; the canon has whitewashed lime and thatch villages and grey ashlar towns.

sheet_or_frame: Board J6: legendary vessels and maritime mysteries
ideas_to_keep: Named ships as world landmarks: a Crown flagship, a Mark raider's longship, an Aurenne explorer, an independent merchant legend that has circled all three islands, an unknown ship seen sailing against the wind before great change. Sea legends: a green spectral ship heard singing in fog, a cursed armada seen before storms, a ship locked in ice in the north, a ship that sails between the world and somewhere else. Strange hulls: a tri-hull explorer, a shallow-draught river and marsh ram, a skysail prototype with angled wing sails, the Living Hull (a ship grown, not built, that answers its crew). Wrecks to dive: a sunken Crown warship, a raider wreck with runes in the hull, the Sunken Library (an Aurenne scholar ship lost with a floating archive), a graveyard of mixed wrecks. Sea places: the Broken Reef, the Whispering Deep (a great whirlpool), the Veiled Isles (appear and vanish with the seasons), the Frozen Reach. Rewards: figureheads, ship blueprints, lost maps, navigational instruments.
notes: Fills the sea's gap for landmarks and legends; the Living Hull and the Veiled Isles are the 'strange, not stock' register. Conflicts: 'Raider King' and Jorund Bloodwake's 'raider clans' (the Mark has no king and scorns the word; the Captains' League), 'Imperial Explorer' (Aurenne is the Compact, not an empire). Ghost ships and the cursed armada are dark: Michael keeps dark imagery for the gates, so these would be rare, eerie rather than grim. The Sunken Library fits Aurenne's academy; wrecks already exist in the game. Names are proposals.

sheet_or_frame: Character creation: variations with a simple creator UI (second pass)
ideas_to_keep: A simple creator panel: a list on the left (race, gender, face, hair, hair colour, skin tone, appearance, confirm), a strip of choices, and a portrait on the right. Six builds of the same kit: default, stout, lean, tall, young, mature (grey hair, weathered). Five body silhouettes, slim to stocky. A hair-and-beard strip (tied back, braided, short). The hero kit as in OG-005 shown in three ruined-city scenes.
notes: Elf, dwarf and half-elf are offered as races; the canon's choice is the four peoples (§2.2), and the Old Blood option is missing. A clearer UI layout than OG-005; both are earlier thinking that the creator should replace with the four peoples. Note §2.2: an Old Blood player's look should be described inconsistently by NPCs.

sheet_or_frame: NPC sheet E7: diverse roots, shared paths (five named travellers)
ideas_to_keep: Five strong NPC looks, each with portrait, turnaround, still life and scene. Zahra al-Mahdi (Aurennais navigator and gate cartographer): dark brown skin, long curly locs, gold hoop earrings and coin necklace, a navy-and-cream coat, a brass compass and charts. Tavio Rusen (Markman monster hunter and guide): scarred, braided, in furs, with a grey wolf at his side and a horned skull among his trophies. Sister Elidan (Gatelander healer and relic keeper): cream and crimson robes, a gentle older face, candles and a reliquary. Khemrik Voss (Old Blood memory keeper): grey skin with gold marks on the face, white hair, a gold circlet, reaching to a glowing blue sigil wheel on a wall; 'You see ruins. I see unfinished sentences.' Marco di Serra (Aurennais merchant patron): dark beard, a velvet coat, a goblet, ships behind.
notes: Fits the direction: warm, painterly, a pleasant world of people. Zahra and Marco fit decision 4 (Arabic and Italian names suit the new fusion; candidates). Khemrik conflicts: he 'interprets' the gates, which the Withdrawal forbids (§3.1, Old Blood may touch but not read), and he has white hair (canon: black). The forbidden reader is close to Varek's own sin, so he could be written as one of the 'awake' (§10a); a candidate, and a question for Michael. Tavio's wolf companion implies an animal-companion system the game does not have.

sheet_or_frame: Armour tiers: ten tiers in three lines (second pass)
ideas_to_keep: As OG-019, with bolder headgear at the top tiers: horned and finned helms for Mithril and Obsidian, a flame crest for Draconic, great curved horns for Demonic, a crescent-and-halo crown for Cosmic; antlered and haloed hoods on the high robes. The light line is masked and hooded from the second tier, which reads as 'rogue'.
notes: Second pass of OG-019. The masks hide the faces in the light and robe rows, and the high tiers lean into dark-lord spikes; OG-019 is the one to keep. Useful for top-tier helm silhouettes.

sheet_or_frame: Character sheet: Aldwyn, Royal Herald of Ironhaven
ideas_to_keep: Three outfits: the formal herald's robe (crimson, with gold embroidery and a gold wheel-and-compass device on the shoulder), the travelling scholar's (charcoal coat, hood, satchel, belt of instruments), the private study's (cream undertunic, red over-robe, a book). Greying dark wavy hair, a short beard, a lined, thoughtful face; expressions: neutral, thoughtful, concerned, a quiet smile. A herald's brooch (the wheel device), a leather satchel, a sigil tattooed on the inside of his wrist. His things: a tooled journal with the wheel on its cover, rolled maps of the gates, a brass astrolabe, a wax seal (canon: he hands the player a Royal Mage Corps wax seal, Q6). Scenes: at court before a crowned king, in the field sketching a ruin.
notes: Crimson and gold matches the Crown (§1.5). He is drawn as a vigorous man of fifty; the canon has him 150+ years in Ironhaven, 'old, physically fragile, and afraid to die', so he should read older and frailer. The wrist sigil 'shared with Varek' would make Aldwyn Old Blood or a reader of the script; the canon does not say, and it fits his 'institution that no longer exists' and the Ald- naming link: a candidate, and a question for Michael. The 'with Varek' panel uses OG-013's off-canon Varek. The quote is invented.

sheet_or_frame: NPC sheet E11: the unexplained (five strange figures)
ideas_to_keep: Five strange-but-friendly figures, Morrowind-style. The Clockwork Pilgrim: a brass-faced construct in a wide straw hat and patched robes with a staff and pack, a chronicler who turns up at important moments ('I walk the same roads as you, but not the same time'). The Rooted One: an old talking tree by a forgotten shrine, bluebirds on its branches. The Veiled Merchant: a cream veil over a gold mask, a stall of impossible goods, who 'knows more about the player than they should'. The Gateborn Companion: a calm, frilled, dragon-like creature in red and blue that bonds with a traveller. The Painted Woman: appears in paintings, murals and crowds across the islands with 'different face, same eyes'.
notes: Answers §10a's 'strange, not stock' directly, and the world gap it names. The Painted Woman echoes the inconsistent descriptions of an Old Blood player (§2.2) and the Veiled Merchant who knows the player suits 'the awake' (§10a): both candidates. The Gateborn Companion conflicts with §5 (gate-born dragons are antibodies that do not speak or bond) and would need a companion system; a question for Michael. The Clockwork Pilgrim implies constructs, which the canon has not placed. The picture is warm and inviting, the register the 12 Oct style call asks for.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet A: the four peoples, overview (first pass)
ideas_to_keep: An emblem per people at the top of each column: a gold compass star (Gatelanders), a green arrowhead-and-leaf (Markmen), a lilac four-pointed star (Aurennais), a red sigil star (Old Blood). Otherwise nothing the people pages lack.
notes: Off-canon for three of four peoples: the Markmen as green-hooded forest scouts and archers (canon: tall, pale, ash-blond, furs, the cold north), the Aurennais as fair, blond, noble scholars in blue (against decision 4), the Old Blood as 'a warrior people' with a big dark-skinned man in furs (canon: short, slight, grey-pale, scattered). The footnote 'Elves and Dwarves are not part of the current canon' is right. Superseded by the people pages OG-048, OG-002, OG-044 and OG-008.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet: the four peoples, Aurennais page
ideas_to_keep: Eight everyday Aurennais in pairs (merchant, farmer, traveller, craftsperson, male and female): cream linen under-tunics, a long patterned sash wrapped over one shoulder, wide sash belts in rust red and indigo, head-wraps and hooded shawls, leather sandals with ankle straps. Skin from tan to deep brown, curly, wavy and braided hair, gold hoop earrings and coin necklaces. Clothing panels: shoulder-draped shawls in olive, red and indigo with block-printed borders. Details: a big gold medallion pendant, bead strings, indigo resist-dyed cloth, a tooled leather belt with hanging coins, a satchel. Palette: saffron, ochre, brick red, indigo, olive, sand. Environment: a palm-lined quay with awnings and a lateen-rigged boat, cream plaster town climbing a hill.
notes: Matches decision 4 (Mediterranean / North African mix, darker skin, a healthy range) far better than canon's olive-to-brown Norman register; the people-table row should be updated to match. The female craftsperson's bare-midriff gold top reads as costume rather than a working woman; drop it. The board's skyline is Italianate; the Egyptian and Arabic notes of decision 4 are thin here (no domes, no geometric tile).

sheet_or_frame: Character sheet E1: five named NPCs (Bram, Edna, Corwin, Niamh, Áine)
ideas_to_keep: Bram: broad, grey-bearded smith in a leather apron, arms folded at the anvil; props family hammer, tongs, an unfinished gate-iron fitting. Edna: white-haired woman in her sixties in layered red and indigo shawls with a walking stick, herbs drying overhead; props herbal satchel, mortar, dried gatebloom. Corwin: lean, grinning merchant in a blue-and-gold coat, boots up on a crate at the quay; props ledger, maps, foreign coins, a mystery vial. Niamh: plain woman in her forties, long braid, fur-collared grey cloak, staff, the sea cave behind her; props watch token, spyglass, tide chart. Áine: woman in her seventies, braid, woven red-and-blue shawl, two hands on a stick, standing stones behind; props family amulet, woven shawl, carved bone keepsake. Three expression heads each.
notes: Earlier pass of OG-069 (same five, same sheet number), which adds turnarounds; keep this one for its prop captions and secrets (Bram turned down a lord's offer in Ironhaven; Edna keeps a relic from a gate; Corwin smuggles; Niamh sees a pattern in travellers; Áine knows more about the Old Blood than she admits). Ages and character notes follow the canon closely (Bram's grandfather's forge, Edna's three gates, Corwin's evasions). Conflict: Niamh and Áine are labelled Markmen, but Carraig Mór and Inis Rua are Irish-coded Gatelands places and their names are Gatelander; treat both as Gatelanders. Corwin labelled Aurennais: canon is silent on his people, so this is a candidate (his name is not Aurennais in register; ask Michael). 'Gatebloom' as a herb name is new; candidate.

sheet_or_frame: Board 15: ports, roads & infrastructure (second pass), with mounts and beasts of burden
ideas_to_keep: Three port kinds: Gatelands river port with ferry crossing, Mark fjord port built into cliffs, Aurennais coastal fishing harbour; a domed Aurennais capital port with red-sailed ships. Waystations: inn, stables, coach house, windmill, watermill, lighthouse, watchtower, carved roadstone/milestone (a knotwork-carved stone at the roadside). Mountain pass with timber trestle roads and guard posts in the Mark. Mounts, one per island: Gatelands Horse (grey, versatile), Mark Steed (dark, shaggy-fetlocked, hardy), Aurennais Courser (chestnut, fast and elegant); Draft Horse; Pack Mule; Mountain Ox (yak-like, used in the Mark for logging and highland transport). Vehicles: traveller's cart, covered wagon, merchant carriage, noble coach, military wagon.
notes: Filed under creatures but it is board 15; OG-046 (the refined pass, in 03_World_Architecture_Transport) supersedes it and OG-007 is the first pass. Its distinct value here is the mount line-up: one horse breed per island, and the ox as the Mark's beast of burden. "Solaris Harbor, Aurenneis capital port" is the generator's name (and spelling). Horses today exist only on coaches; riding is not built.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet: the four peoples, Gatelanders page
ideas_to_keep: Eight everyday Gatelanders: villager with a pitchfork, tradesperson in a long leather apron, traveller/ranger with bow and short cloak, Crown guards in a red-and-gold tabard with a gold sun-cross, kettle helm and spear. Wiry, freckled, red to dark-brown hair, weathered cheeks. Kit: short red shoulder capes held by round brass cloak pins, many belt pouches, laced boots and leg wraps, embroidered hems, headscarves on women, a basket. Material swatches: red wool, brown leather, moss green, sea blue, linen, iron. Palette: earth, stone, red clay, deep green, sea blue, with Crown red and gold for guards and officials.
notes: Fits canon §2 (fair to ruddy, freckled, dark or red hair, wiry). Crown red-and-gold matches canon §1.5. The skyline is a grey ashlar town with a bridge; fine. Whole board leans red; in game the countryside folk should carry more of the green, undyed and blue than shown. Pairs with OG-056.

sheet_or_frame: Key frame 5 variant: the gate, low sun
ideas_to_keep: Concentric-ring gate in warmer light, standing stone in the foreground.
notes: Variant of OG-037.

sheet_or_frame: Board 13: Aurenne, settlements and life
ideas_to_keep: Terraced domed harbour capital with aqueducts; settlement kinds: coastal town, cliff village, oasis settlement, desert outpost, hillside town (olives, vineyards), island monastery-port. Daily life: spice markets, shaded garden courtyards with fountains, camel caravans. Style: domes and arches, blue glazed tilework, carved stone, lattice screens, courtyards, columns and arcades, banners by house and guild. Buildings: townhouse, merchant house, courtyard home, temple, palace. Materials: limestone, glazed tile, cypress and cedar, linen, bronze and brass, pottery and glass, spices and dyes.
notes: Names (Solaris, Talassa, Zahir, Qamar, Al-Nuri, Siraa) follow a North African register; the canon gives Aurenne Norman-French names. "Royal courts and palaces" conflicts with the Compact (merchant houses under the Church). Look fits the canon: cream plaster, tiled roofs, arcades, domes, warehouses on every quay.

sheet_or_frame: Bestiary: game monsters grouped by the six old dungeon themes, each with a hall vignette
ideas_to_keep: Details not on the other bestiaries: the Mimic shown closed as an ordinary iron-bound chest beside its open form (the tell must be small); the Kobold Thief as a rat-faced, hunched, cloaked creature rather than a small goblin, which separates it from the Goblin at a glance; the Slime splitting into small slimes; a deep Cave Troll with violet fungus growing from its back; a deep Golem of dark stone with blue crystal growths; a deep Slime drawn as a tall jellyfish bell with trailing threads; the ruins Golem built half into a standing wall; a goblin chief with a crested skull helm. Each row ends on a small vignette of a lone figure in that gate's hall.
notes: Organised by the old six themes, which §9a replaced with the schools; OG-018 (by school) and OG-073 (by condition) supersede it as layouts. Keep for the individual designs above. A rat-faced kobold departs from the game's current kobold; Michael's call.

sheet_or_frame: Combat key frame: sword and spell against a skeleton (pass with crossed blades, tighter)
ideas_to_keep: As OG-045, framed tighter: an X of blades at the centre with a burst of sparks, the spell held in the off hand at the frame edge, a second skeleton advancing with a round shield, ring-and-line glyphs on the piers.
notes: Pass of OG-011; near duplicate of OG-045 (slightly better spacing).

sheet_or_frame: Sheet E10: guildmasters and power brokers
ideas_to_keep: Five guild heads, each with turnaround, props and a scene. Lady Corvina Draeth, Aurennais merchant prince: dark skin, cream head-wrap and robe with gold embroidery, gold cuffs; scales, ledgers, seals. Master Haldrin, Gatelander grand artisan: white-bearded, leather and brass, tools and plans. High Archmage Selene: dark hair, midnight-blue robe with gold stars, a floating sigil ring of light over her hand. Ser Jorren Vale, Fighters' Guild: red cape and surcoat over plate, a guild banner with a gold sword; bounty notices. Matriarch Ysara, healers' circle: old woman in a green floral wrap, herbs and remedies, a deer beside her. Each has a hook line (Corvina 'can open doors anywhere for a price'; Jorren 'contracts and protection or a bounty on your head').
notes: Names, titles and the healers' circle are the generator's; proposals. Canon puts the Mages' academy in Aurenne, so its head being 'mixed (Markman heritage)' is possible but should be checked; the Fighters' Guild is half Markish in canon, so a Gatelander knight at its head is a choice to make. 'Master of Coin' and 'merchant prince' fit the Compact's houses (canon §1.3). A cross-island healers' circle answerable to no nation fills a gap; candidate. Corvina's look is a strong Aurennais elite under decision 4.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet E3: five new faces (townsfolk)
ideas_to_keep: Fen Oisín, Gatelander stablemaster: round-faced, cheerful, leather vest, with a bay horse; saddlebags, horseshoes, a lantern. Bronwen, Markman fisher and cartographer: grey-haired woman in a net-draped shawl, charts and a spyglass. Perrin, tinker and scrapsmith: wild hair, round spectacles, brass gears and clockwork birds on his bench. Síle, Old Blood midwife and storykeeper: grey-pale skin, white braided hair, sigil tattoos across face and hands, plum robe, a carved knotwork staff; herbs, a red book, a mortar. Garrick, disabled veteran and gatewarden: scarred, bearded, fur-collared, seated in a wheeled chair on a headland wall with a black wolfhound.
notes: Síle is a good Old Blood elder (grey-pale, tattooed); canon puts the tattoos at the wrists, and here they cover face and hands: decide whether the elders wear more. Her white hair is age, not a break with the black-hair rule. Perrin is labelled Aurennais but drawn fair; under decision 4 recolour him. Garrick holds a long gun like a musket: canon has no firearms; give him a crossbow. Bronwen's name is Welsh-register for a Markman; the Mark's names are Anglo (canon §2).

sheet_or_frame: Sheet: the four peoples, Old Blood page (pass with embedded sigils)
ideas_to_keep: Sigils drawn as raised, pale lines under the skin of the wrist, the back of the hand and the shoulder blade, branching like veins, rather than ink. Clothing: dark, asymmetric layers over cream undyed linen with a scattered dot embroidery, a single shoulder wrap, a round stone-and-iron amulet on the belt, belts with small hanging charms. Muted palette of bone white, ash, slate, oxblood and a dusk violet. An eye strip (pale grey, silver, ice blue) as a reference for the Cold's greying eyes.
notes: Conflicts with canon §2–3 on the body: drawn tall, lean and long-limbed, most with white or silver hair and some violet or black eyes, with 'subtle non-human features', i.e. elvish. Canon is short, slight, grey-pale, black hair, sigils at the wrist; and they are scattered through the three peoples, not 'isolated clans' in the highlands with gothic castles. Keep only the skin, the embedded-sigil treatment (which reads well at game scale and could carry the Cold) and the clothes. Whether the marks are tattoos or under the skin is a question for Michael. Second Old Blood pass alongside OG-067; neither is right.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet: the four peoples, Old Blood page (pass with tattoos and furs)
ideas_to_keep: Eight Old Blood at work (hunter, herdsman, stoneworker, healer, scholar, clan elder): layered dark wool over undyed linen printed with small scattered marks, fur collars, a round brooch pinning a shoulder cape, belts of pouches and charms, carved bone and stone pendants. Face tattoos as thin lines at the temple and brow. Environment panel: people gathered at a ring of tall standing stones and a ruined tower by a lake, a fire in the middle; a good picture of where the Old Blood keep their tongue.
notes: Conflicts with canon §2–3: tall builds, blond and grey hair, blue and green eyes, isolated highland clans. Canon is short, slight, grey-pale, black hair, scattered among the islands and married into them. The black-haired, braided woman (top-right face, 'herdswoman') is the nearest to canon. Earlier or sister pass of OG-066; a corrected Old Blood page is still owed.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet 11: the Gatelands (first pass)
ideas_to_keep: Settlement kinds: small village, market town, river settlement (mills), coastal town, fortified keep, ancient Weaver ruins reclaimed by nature. Typical buildings: cottage, farmhouse, tavern, blacksmith, alchemy shop, trader, temple, guildhall, watchtower. Motifs: rounded arches, knotwork carving, crown banners, nature motifs. Materials: limestone, thatch, slate, timber, wattle and daub, ironwork lanterns. Harbour life, market square, rural life with sheep and cattle.
notes: Superseded by OG-070. Calls the Gatelands "the northern island"; canon has it south.

sheet_or_frame: Character sheet E1 (refined): Bram, Edna, Corwin, Niamh, Áine with turnarounds
ideas_to_keep: The same five as OG-057 with front, side and back turnarounds, prop tables and a scene each. Bram: barrel-chested, short dark beard, rolled sleeves, leather apron, arms folded; props hammers, tongs, anvil. Edna: white hair in a bun, a clay pipe, dark green shawl over layers, a stick; satchel, mortar, a hammer, a little bottle. Corwin: dark curls, grin, red-and-gold coat over a waistcoat, tankard in hand; coin purse, compass, strongbox. Niamh: dark wind-blown hair, black hooded cloak with a round brooch, a lantern at the cave mouth; horn, lantern, tide map. Áine: long white braid, deep red wrap with a woven border, two hands on a carved stick; woven blanket, a ringed stone disc, a cup, marigolds. Lines: Bram 'A good tool outlives its maker'; Niamh 'I don't stop what comes through. I remember it.'
notes: Supersedes OG-057 for the models (turnarounds); OG-057 keeps its prop captions and secrets. Áine is a Gatelander here (correct). Niamh is still labelled Markman: she is Gatelander (Inis Rua, Irish-coded). Corwin's people is given as 'Aurenne': canon is silent; a candidate for Michael. Bram is drawn younger and dark-bearded where OG-057 has him grey; canon has him at the forge thirty years, so grey fits better. Niamh 'watches the Gate at Inis Rua' fits canon (the Mouth).

sheet_or_frame: Board 11: the Gatelands, settlements and life (refined)
ideas_to_keep: Capital on seven hills where a river meets the sea: harbour, market district, great cathedral, royal keep. Village: whitewashed thatch, field walls, village green. River town with mills; coastal town with a small fort; hill town reusing ancient Weaver stonework. Irish-inspired details: thatched whitewashed cottage, field walls, rounded arches, high crosses with knotwork, slate roofs in towns, harp trade signs, banners (tree, wave, crown). Buildings: cottage, townhouse, merchant house with shop, warehouse. Materials: limestone, granite, thatch, oak/ash/birch, slate, pottery, wool and linen, ironwork, wood carving.
notes: Calls the capital "Crownhaven"; canon seats the Crown at Coeur de Vie, in pale stone and terracotta.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet E4: five unusual souls
ideas_to_keep: Tomcán, fool and oracle: patchwork jester's coat and hood with bells, a raven on his shoulder, a mask among his props; turns up where he shouldn't and 'speaks to your shadow'. Nell, beastkeeper: curly-haired woman with a huge, gentle tusked beast like a walrus-beaver; she heals what others fear. Elias, collector of forgotten things: goggles, a brass armillary sphere, a coat hung with trinkets and a pack piled high. Branwen, the Rooted One: an Old Blood hermit overgrown with moss, bark and ivy, green-grey skin, a bird on her shoulder, living at the foot of a great tree; feathers, mushrooms and herbs. Orvin, tide poet and ferryman: weathered, pipe, broad hat, a lantern and a heron at his boat.
notes: Strong on the 'strange, not stock' line of canon §10a. Branwen's rooted, half-plant Old Blood is a fresh idea, but canon's Cold turns readers grey and cold, not green; decide whether she is a reader gone strange another way, or a Gaoth/Cloch oddity. Elias is labelled Aurennais but drawn pale; recolour under decision 4. Nell's beast is unnamed; a candidate creature. Orvin as a Markman ferryman between islands fits the sea as a road.

sheet_or_frame: Board J2: player ships and progression
ideas_to_keep: Player ship ladder with level bands: fishing boat (starter, 8 to 12 m, crew 1 to 4), coastal sloop (early), merchant cog (mid), brigantine (late), frigate (end, 35 m and up, crew 30 to 60). Hull style by island: Gatelands rounded, sturdy, elegant timberwork; Mark clinker-built and reinforced; Aurenne sleek, lateen-rigged, ornate. Sail options: square, fore-and-aft, lateen, mixed rig. Customisation: hull shape and paint, figureheads, banners and heraldry, wear and repairs, mast and sail sets with regional patterns and furled or reefed states; armaments; functional upgrades (helm, anchor, larger hold, crew quarters, crafting stations). A cutaway of a mid-game cog labelled by deck: upper deck helm, navigation table, crew stations, cannons optional; main deck cargo and companionway; below deck personal room, storage and crafting, bed. Below-deck variants by play style: explorer (simple), trader (storage), adventurer (crafting), captain (luxury). Deck layouts for sloop, cog, brigantine.
notes: The progression board; pairs with OG-027 (interiors). 'Cannons (optional)' on the upper deck agrees with Michael's note better than OG-017; the frigate is the natural home for them. The rig and wear options line up with sailing.md's rig bar and the sail tiers already in the game (shipTopSpeed). Class ladder differs from the game's five: a decision.

sheet_or_frame: Bestiary: gate failure variants, one monster per school at steady, failing and catastrophic
ideas_to_keep: Gate condition drawn as three states of one monster: steady ("familiar forms, coherent"), failing ("distorted anatomy, signs of the gate"), catastrophic ("unbound, otherworldly"). Tine: Fire Elemental grows a stone skeleton inside its flame, then becomes a towering fire titan. Uisce: Slime multiplies into a cresting wave of jelly, then a vast spectral water mass. Cloch: Golem doubles into a pair, then an exploded golem with floating plates and blue light in its cracks. Scáth: Wraith spreads more rags and limbs, then a many-armed violet shade. Solas: Skeleton grows extra arms and spines, then a many-armed skeleton with a light halo. Gaoth: Gargoyle grows bigger wings and more limbs, then a storm-wrapped winged thing. The failing column is the useful one: the same model with extra limbs and broken anatomy, which a build can make from one rig.
notes: Draws Part I and §9a's "condition sets the strangeness". Canon makes the catastrophic case a dragon (§5), one per failure; this sheet proposes a catastrophic form of every monster, which would be a boss tier under the dragon. Decision for Michael. The catastrophic forms glow all over, against the monster rule (familiar silhouette, built wrong, glow only at seams); the failing forms follow it better. The top strip shows the gate itself darkening red then violet; the gate is drawn as a gothic arch, not concentric rings.

sheet_or_frame: Overview: the four peoples, one pair each
ideas_to_keep: Only the Aurennais pair is worth a look: blue, white and gold formal dress with a round gold sun-compass brooch, matching the Compact's blue-and-white.
notes: An early overview that misses the canon on three of four peoples: Gatelanders and Markmen are near-identical leather-and-green rangers (Markmen should be tall, broad, pale, ash-blond); Aurennais are 'lighter skin tones', against decision 4; Old Blood are 'strong, sturdy', fur-clad, braided and blond. The note 'Elves and dwarves are not part of the current canon' is right. Superseded by the per-people pages (OG-056, OG-059 and the others).

sheet_or_frame: Board K2: legendary and unique weapons
ideas_to_keep: Five legendary weapons per island in its style (Gatelands: a longsword of the first king, a lightning war axe, a forest wardens' spear, a mace with ever-burning embers, a ranger's longbow; Mark: a great axe, an ice-glacier two-hander, a whaling harpoon that pulls foes, a chain flail, a ritual spear; Aurenne: a duellist's rapier, a meteor-steel scimitar, a composite bow, a tide-blessed crescent blade, a dancer's war fan). Gate relics from before the islands: a greatsword engraved with gate runes, a dagger that drinks sound, a hammer of a vanished mountain-shaping people, a spear said to have opened the first gate, a staff with a ruined civilisation set in it. Where legendaries are found: in ruins, in royal houses, in shipwrecks, behind trials. Each legendary given a distinct silhouette, rich material and a visible magic effect.
notes: Details only. Names, owners and stat lines (life steal, bonus vs humans, sanity drain) are invented and MMO-flavoured. 'The Black Compass' is a flintlock pistol: guns in hand are not in the canon or the brief and are a decision for Michael. 'Saint Brigid's Flame' uses a real saint's name. 'Bloodwake ... united the raider clans' puts a king-figure on the Mark. The gate relics touch the Makers and the gates' origin, which canon controls. The cursed row (The Hunger, The Bone Tide) is dark imagery outside the gates.

sheet_or_frame: Combat key frame: sword and spell against a skeleton (pass with shield on the back)
ideas_to_keep: As OG-011, darker: the player carries a round shield slung on the back while casting into the skeleton's chest; the ring-and-cross glyph repeated down the hall as a lit sigil door at the far end.
notes: Pass of OG-011. The lit ring-and-cross door at the end of the hall is a good sigil-door idea.

sheet_or_frame: Key frame 2: the Gatelands, with a hare post-rider
ideas_to_keep: The final key frame 2: a huge Weaver ruin (pillars and arch) on the skyline as the landmark, river town with bridge and church, lighthouse on the coast, sheep in walled fields, autumn trees, and a post rider on a horse-sized hare: the brief's creative-licence seed, made ordinary.
notes: Best image of the batch for the brief's tone.

sheet_or_frame: Key frame 5 variant: the gate, lakeside
ideas_to_keep: Concentric-ring gate above a lake, closer framing.
notes: Variant of OG-037.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet H1: five legendary figures
ideas_to_keep: The Salt King, smuggler and folk hero: long dark hair, red and blue sea coat, gold chains, a lantern on a night quay; feeds starving villages and runs blockades. Sister Cairde, the Gatewalker: hooded cream robe spattered with red, satchel and candles; has been through more gates than anyone and came back changed; her scene has her at a lit ring-gate. Red Finn, the cursed champion: red-bearded, bare-chested and tattooed, fur over one shoulder, a greatsword; undefeated in the arenas, changed after a massacre on the Blackshore isle. The Hollow Bard: gold half-mask, feathered hat, a lute; trades stories for stories. The Wretched Abbot: shaven, gaunt, a thorn circlet, white and gold vestments with chains; led an order that tried to preserve the gates and broke something.
notes: Names, the Blackshore isle and the arenas are the generator's; proposals. The Salt King fits canon's piracy as the Mark's undeclared war and the Compact's tithe-ships as prey. The Wretched Abbot echoes the Church of the Weaver blessing the dead into the gates without knowing the price (canon §3.1); a candidate for an awake character. Red Finn is labelled Markman with red hair: Markmen are ash-blond in canon. Sister Cairde is labelled Aurennais but drawn fair with an Irish name; recolour under decision 4 or make her a Gatelander. Her scene's ring-gate is a useful nod to the V1 rings.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet E1 (alternate): five new faces, townsfolk
ideas_to_keep: Tomas, ferrymaster and boatwright: big, red-bearded, laughing, tankard in hand, rope and a lantern; rowing boat, oars, lantern among his props. A forager-apothecary: dark curls under a red headscarf, green shawl, an armful of wildflowers; basket, bottles, mortar, scissors. Father Eamon, itinerant priest: grey beard, red-and-cream vestments, a tall brass crook topped with a ring; a book with a cross-and-circle cover, a censer. Jora, arena trainer: dark-skinned woman with long locs pulled back, sleeveless leather and arm wraps; staves, a round shield, training gear. Rivel, mapmaker and chronicler: young, round spectacles, scarf, ink-stained, with rolled charts and an astrolabe.
notes: Earlier pass of OG-089 (same five), which dresses Jora as a Markman. Keep this one for Jora as a dark-skinned, locs-wearing trainer, a good Aurennais or port-town look. The forager is named Sera, which canon already gives to Ashenmoor's guard; rename. 'Sheet E1' repeats the label of OG-057/OG-069, a generator slip. Jora is labelled 'The Mark' and drawn dark-skinned: Markmen are tall, pale, ash-blond, though canon §1.5 allows a mixed crowd in a port; make her Aurennais or note her as a port-born mix. Rivel and the forager are labelled Aurenne but drawn fair; recolour under decision 4. Arenas are not in canon; a candidate (it also appears in OG-079). The priest's crook and ring icon could carry the Church of the Weaver; ask which church he serves.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet E13: children and young people
ideas_to_keep: Lirien of Saltsong, harbour urchin: dark-skinned Aurennais girl with braided hair, red scarf, gold earrings, spyglass and shells; knows every smugglers' landing. Tomas Ironvein, would-be knight: freckled red-haired Gatelander boy with a wooden practice sword and a too-big helmet. Naya of the Embers, gifted apprentice: Old Blood girl with sigil marks on her face, sigil rings of light spinning over her hands, at the Mages' Guild. Bellen and Kiri, sibling scavengers: two grinning boys and a scruffy dog, a bag of salvage. Sera Valeth, the reluctant heir: noble girl in a cream and blue gown with gold embroidery who slips out to see the city. Each with turnarounds and props at child scale.
notes: Fills a real gap: the towns have few children (only Finn in Ashenmoor). Naya is Old Blood with white hair and pale violet light; canon gives black hair. Her 'sensitivity to Gate-born magic' fits canon §3.3 (warm stones felt at a distance) and the Withdrawal's ban on reading; a candidate for a quest about a child who reads. Sera Valeth collides with canon's Sera; rename. 'House Valeth' as a Gatelands noble house is a candidate; check against the Crown's lords.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet E2: five new faces, townsfolk
ideas_to_keep: Mairead, innkeeper and storyteller: stout, laughing, red-cheeked, shawl and apron, a pewter tankard; runs the Salt and Lantern. Darragh, gravekeeper and stonemason: hooded, white-bearded, a carved cross-stone behind him, chisels and a lantern; reads old carvings. Iliana, shipwright and salvager: strong, tattooed forearms, red headscarf, adze and plane, a hull on the stocks behind her. Brother Caelen, sceptic priest: young, dark-haired, black hooded habit over white, a book and chalice; 'Faith isn't certainty.' Lyra, herbalist and hunter: red-haired woman in a green hooded cloak with a bow, a basket of purple flowers, a deer in her scene.
notes: The Salt and Lantern is placed 'at the Ashenmoor pier'; Ashenmoor in canon is a farming village, not a port, so move it (Salthaven fits the name). Iliana works 'the Ironhaven docks': check that Ironhaven has a harbour. Darragh (Irish name) and Lyra are labelled Markmen; canon's Markish names are Anglo and their look ash-blond. Brother Caelen is labelled Aurenne and drawn fair; recolour under decision 4. A gravekeeper who reads carvings is a natural lead to the Clearing (canon §3.1).

sheet_or_frame: Sheet E9: rival adventurers and guilds
ideas_to_keep: Koran Stonehand, mountain guide and gate-clearer: bearded, fur and heavy leather in snow, a pick, a mountain banner. Lyn Étrël, explorer and antiquities broker: dark-skinned Aurennais woman with locs, cream and blue explorer's coat, rolled maps and an orrery. A Gatelander scout with a big grey wolf companion. Sir Alaric Drake, fallen knight: blond, red cloak and surcoat with a gold lion, a great helm. Zurik the Seventh, Old Blood seeker: cracked grey stone-like skin, white hair, black robe with gold stars, a brass armillary. Rival adventurers with hooks (a high-risk expedition, a guide for hire, a rival for glory) is a good idea for gate-clearers in the world.
notes: Names the scout 'Varek' (Varek & Moss): the villain's name is reserved, so this must be renamed. Zurik's cracked, statue-like skin and white hair push the Old Blood toward non-human; canon is grey-pale, black-haired, human. Koran is labelled Markman and drawn dark-skinned and short-haired; Markmen are pale and ash-blond. Lyn Étrël is a strong Aurennais under decision 4, though the diaeresis name has the dropped Norman-French ring. Rival adventurers fill a gap (the salvage economy of canon §1.1); candidate.

sheet_or_frame: Field guide: fauna of the three islands, 45 island species, common species, and marine life
ideas_to_keep: The one-page roster across all three islands and the sea. Markish Highlands: Stone Goat, Snow Hare, Ironwolf, Crag Bear, Sky Eagle, Peak Ibex, Frost Lynx, Mountain Ptarmigan, Glacial Marmot, Ridge Stag, Alpine Salamander, Stonecrawler, Highcliff Falcon, Blizzard Fox, Rock Trout. Central Gatelands: Gatefen Boar, Redspine Fox, Eldertree Deer, River Otter, Great Heron, Woodland Badger, Greenward Stoat, Hollowcat, Barred Owl, Thicket Boar, Grove Turkey, Tree Runner (a small songbird), Marsh Frog, Painted Turtle, Common Carp. Aurennais Coast: Saltskim Seal, Sand Gazelle, Dune Cat, Cliffhawk, Coastal Ibex, Sea Goat, Sunshell Tortoise, Marsh Heron, Oasis Hare, Striped Hyena, Sand Skink, Carmine Kingfisher, Coastal Crab, Duneswift, Reef Lizard. All islands: wolf, red fox, brown hare, raven, crow, wild boar, deer, badger, otter, trout: the shared base set that can be built once and recoloured. Marine life: harbour seal, grey dolphin, Storm Whale, sailfin ray, Drifter Jelly (glowing), giant octopus, tidecrab, reef moray, Lantern Fish (glowing, deep), Gate Eel (dark, with a glowing line along its length), coastal tuna, swordfish, shellfish, sea turtle, coral stalk. Gate Leviathan: a colossal whale-shaped thing seen past a sunken wreck, glowing seams down its body, "said to follow the currents between worlds" (a rare sea encounter or sighting).
notes: Overview companion to the island sheets OG-009, OG-031, OG-030 (which carry the detail and more of the strange names); this one adds the marine life the game is thin on (it has fish, gulls, dolphins, whales and sharks) and the shared common set. The Gate Leviathan and Gate Eel fit the antibody canon only if they come from a gate in the sea (the Mouth, the Vault of the Tide): a sea gate's antibodies, glowing at the seams. "Between worlds" is the generator's phrase and not canon. Some species repeat across islands with new names (ibex, goat, stag, falcon); pick one name per animal.

sheet_or_frame: Bestiary: familiar, corrupted and gate beings (first pass)
ideas_to_keep: Three rows. Familiar: wolf, bear, stag, boar, a raptor bird, giant spider, scorpion, troll, goblin with spear, skeleton with round shield, wraith. Corrupted: the same animals with glowing seams, crystal growths and violet light (corrupted wolf, bear, deer, rot boar, shadow raptor, blood scorpion, fallen troll, goblin shaman, bone wraith). Gate beings: the Gate Warden (a tall armoured figure with a halo-ring), Realm Hound, Void Serpent, the Watcher (a floating eye in a cage of tendrils), Ashen Colossus, the Hollow (a thin figure in a halo), Dread Matron, Obelisk Guardian (crystal plates), the Maw (a ringed toothed worm). A strip of element orbs (violet, green, blue, orange) as variants.
notes: Earlier pass of OG-088, which is clearer. Every corrupted creature is the same violet glow; canon §9a has each gate's antibodies take its school's shape, so the glow should follow the school (Tine ember, Uisce frost, Cloch crystal and stone, and so on). Glowing seams match the Faolchú of a sudden failure (canon, Act I). The hero gate at the top is a tall pointed arch, not the concentric rings of decision 2. Belongs to the creatures folder in spirit.

sheet_or_frame: Character study: Varek (dark-lord pass)
ideas_to_keep: Little to take. The props only: a stack of worn notebooks with a sigil on the cover, loose pages of hand-drawn sigil diagrams, a brass armillary instrument, a metal stylus. The 'hand and sigils' detail (fine marks across the back of the hand) could serve the Old Blood wrist script.
notes: Contradicts the canon on almost every line. Varek is short, slight, grey-pale, black-haired, grey-eyed, in plain dark charcoal clothes, and never a dark lord; here he is tall, gaunt, bald, with a scarred scalp, in a tattered floating robe, levitating before a glowing portal, with Vader, Voldemort, Dagoth Ur and Thanos as the stated mood. That is the reading canon §10a rules out ('faces, town layouts and Varek stay familiar'). The portal behind him is a pointed arch, not the V1 rings. The same figure reappears in OG-092's 'With Varek' panel. A new Varek sheet is owed.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet: the four peoples, Gatelanders page (first pass)
ideas_to_keep: Six Gatelanders (adventurer/ranger, soldier/guard, craftsman/tradesperson, male and female) in brown leather and a deep blue wool. Head variations with headbands and braids. Details: a round blue shield painted with a gold tree, a blue hood with a gold-stitched border, buckled boots, belts of pouches. Culture panel: a river town of grey stone and timber with boats at a quay.
notes: Earlier pass of OG-059, which is closer to the canon (freckled, wiry, Crown red-and-gold on the guards). Here the guards wear blue rather than the Crown's crimson and gold (canon §1.5), and 'strong, sturdy build' is against canon's wiry Gatelanders. The tree emblem recurs on OG-095; it has no place in canon yet.

sheet_or_frame: Bestiary: creatures of the Gatelands (familiar, corrupted, gate-born)
ideas_to_keep: Seven per row, each with a head study and a silhouette. Familiar: wolf, boar, red deer, grizzly, giant eagle, a mossy river troll, giant spider. Corrupted, each a clear shape change rather than a recolour: corrupted wolf with glowing seams, blight boar with crystal spikes in its hide, stag of shadows whose antlers breathe a mist, frost wraith bear of blue ice, dusk eagle with draining violet feathers, stone troll fused with rock, void spider. Gate-born: gate worm (a ringed toothed maw), sky leviathan (a winged ribbed skeleton-fish), shattered colossus (floating stone fragments held as a body), the Hollow (a thin figure under a halo-ring), Bridgeshaper (a tangle of limbs that bends distance), the Echo (a cloud of eyes and voices), the Ascended (a radiant crystal figure).
notes: Supersedes OG-085. The corrupted row maps well onto canon §9a's schools: frost bear for Uisce, crystal boar and stone troll for Cloch, stag of shadows for Scáth, dusk eagle and sky leviathan for Gaoth; propose tagging each with its school. 'Corrupted by Gate energy' should read as the gate's antibodies (Part I, the central mystery). 'Feeds on mana' and the Ascended as 'the original inhabitants' contradict the canon (the Weavers made the gates; there is no mana); drop those lines. The silhouettes are directly useful for the creature kit (34-creatures.js).

sheet_or_frame: Sheet E1 (refined alternate): five new faces, townsfolk
ideas_to_keep: The same five as OG-080 with a cleaner hand. Tomas, laughing red-bearded ferrymaster with a tankard, boat, oars and lantern. A forager-apothecary in a red headscarf and green shawl with wildflowers. Father Eamon, grey-bearded itinerant priest in red and cream with a tall brass ringed crook, a book and censer. Jora, now a Markman arena trainer in a big fur mantle, braided hair, a round red shield with a white cross-ring, training staves; 'runs the training grounds in a Markish coastal town'. Rivel, bespectacled young mapmaker in a cream coat with rolled charts and an astrolabe.
notes: Supersedes OG-080 (Jora is now dressed and placed as a Markman, closer to canon). Still owed: the forager is named Sera, which canon gives Ashenmoor's guard; Rivel and the forager are labelled Aurenne but drawn fair (decision 4); Jora's dark braided hair against canon's ash-blond Markmen. Training grounds or arenas in the Mark fit its duels and mercenary trade (canon §1.2); candidate.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet E12: families, feuds and dynasties
ideas_to_keep: House Velasco, Aurennais nobility: a dark-skinned woman in white with gold and teal embroidery, gold jewellery, a domed city with palms behind; family turnaround of all ages; ledgers, an astrolabe, a blue house banner. The Ironmere Clan, Markish: red-bearded men in heavy furs, an axe, a blue banner, a fire on a rocky shore; holds passes, mines and shipyards, with a blood feud with a neighbouring clan. The Caelmont House, Gatelander landed family: plate under a blue cloak with a gold lion, a plumed helm, a sealed letter; keeps roads and harvests for the Crown. The Sorrowvale Lines, Old Blood heritage 'scattered among the islands': pale, white-haired, dark robes; keep artefacts and fragments. The Redmarsh Syndicate: smugglers in red sashes and headscarves among ships and lanterns.
notes: Fills a gap: the canon has nations but few named families. Velasco's look and city fit decision 4 well (domes, palms, darker skin). The Sorrowvale Old Blood are again white-haired (canon: black hair) but correctly scattered among the islands. Ironmere's feud fits the Mark (duels, no king), but a 'truce with the Crown' needs checking against the cold peace of canon §1.4. Caelmont wears blue and a gold lion; the Crown's colours are crimson and gold. All names are proposals; a Spanish-register Velasco suits the dropped Norman naming.

sheet_or_frame: Sheet E8: faith, cults and prophets
ideas_to_keep: Mother Amani, the Lantern of Ash: dark-skinned Aurennais priestess in a white head-cloth and white, blue and gold robes, a tall staff topped with a caged lantern; tends the sick and reads the gates as passage and renewal. Brother Alain, the Iron Sermon: hooded inquisitor in white with a red cross, who hunts unlicensed gate exploration. Shevra the Drowned, tide oracle: wild braids, salt-crusted robes hung with shells, a staff of driftwood, bones and a lantern; reads storms for fishers and smugglers. Father Calix, the Smiling Lamb: a radiant, open-armed cult leader with a sunburst halo, masks among his props; preaches the gates as transcendence through sacrifice. The Veiled Child: a slight grey figure under a white veil, tending abandoned shrines at the gate sites.
notes: The Church of the Weaver is Aurennais in canon and calls gate salvage sacrilege (canon §1.3); Brother Alain's hunt for 'unauthorized exploration' fits it, but he is labelled Gatelander: make him Aurennais or a Gatelander convert. A Markish shaman sits against the Mark's scorn of priests (canon §1.2): a tide-reader rather than a priest would fit. Father Calix's sacrifice cult edges into the grim; keep him as one of the awake or a villain, never the surface tone. The Veiled Child is Old Blood with white hair and glowing eyes; canon is black-haired and human. Mother Amani is the strongest Aurennais priest look so far.

sheet_or_frame: Character study: Aldwyn, Royal Herald of Ironhaven
ideas_to_keep: A lean man of middle years, long dark hair going grey, short beard, tired eyes. Long dark layered robe and scarf over a belted tunic, a satchel, a ring-clasp at the chest, a book always under his arm. Clothing layers as three states: base (shirt and trousers), travel (hooded robe), herald formal (with a long embroidered stole). Four expressions: neutral, thoughtful, concerned, quiet smile. Props: a leather journal with a sigil on the cover, rolled maps of the gates, brass measuring instruments, a hand-drawn map. Line: 'Some things are older than kingdoms. Our work is to remember them.'
notes: Good fit for canon's scholar-mage hiding as a herald. Two flags. A wrist sigil is drawn and captioned 'shared with Varek'; wrist script is the Old Blood mark (canon §2), so this would make Aldwyn Old Blood or a reader who took the mark; that is a story decision for Michael, not a costume note. His 'herald formal' dress has no Crown crimson and gold; a public herald should wear the Crown's colours over the scholar's robe. The 'With Varek' panel uses the dark-lord Varek of OG-086; ignore it.

sheet_or_frame: Board J5: maritime professions and factions
ideas_to_keep: Sailors in each island's dress: Gatelands green coats and tricorn officers; Mark furs, leather and fur-trimmed raiders; Aurenne blue and white, sashes, turbans and headwraps (the Mediterranean and North African register). Hireable crew roles with portraits: captain, first mate, navigator, boatswain, gunner, carpenter (repairs), cook (food and morale), medic, naturalist, mage (arcane support), quartermaster. Crew morale from food, pay, safe voyages, victories, comfortable quarters, leadership, success. Port trades: shipwrights, dock workers, tavern keepers (rumours, crew, contracts), quartermasters, brokers, bounty hunters, ship chandlers, black market. Gear: cutlasses, boarding axes, harpoons, spears, navigation tools, telescope (high tier), charts, rope and rigging, sailcloth; light artillery marked high tier. A busy port market scene.
notes: Artillery and the telescope marked high tier agrees with Michael's cannon note. Factions conflict with canon: 'Gatelands Merchants' League' (merchant houses are Aurenne's Compact), 'Mark War Fleets: clans and jarls' (the Captains' League, no king), 'Aurenne Imperial Fleet' (no empire). 'Aurenne Trade Consortium' is the Compact by another name: lean in. Salvagers and Wreckers fit the Gatelands' salvage economy; Explorers' and Navigators' Guilds fill a gap. The skull-and-crossbones pirate flag needs a world-own mark. The carpenter crew role fits sailing.md's Joinery repairs.

sheet_or_frame: Board K3: magical implements by school
ideas_to_keep: One school per column with an emblem, a colour and four implements: Uisce blue with a crescent moon (tidecaller staff, moonpearl wand, stormglass orb, tome); Cloch brown with a mountain (stoneheart maul, runebound staff, geomancer's foci cubes, tome); Scáth purple with an eye (nightweave staff, veil dagger, umbral lens orb, tome); Solas gold with a sun (sunspire staff, dawnshard wand, beacon sigil, tome); Gaoth grey with a spiral (skyrunner staff, zephyr wand, gale ring, tome). Implement types: staffs, wands, tomes, orbs and foci, ritual pieces (astrolabe, chalice, hourglass), off-hand hybrids (rings, gauntlets, lantern). Notable objects: a gate compass that reveals gates, a quill that replays memories, a chalice that makes water, a stormwhistle used by Aurenne navigators to call wind, a black mirror, a self-writing book. Cultural styles: Gatelands wood, bone and leather; Mark stone, iron and weathered; Aurenne fine metal and carving. Magic in daily life: healing, navigating by stars, lighting homes and ports.
notes: Tine is drawn as life and nature (green leaf, druids, healers): wrong. Tine is fire; this board's Solas takes 'fire' too. Its Tine column (rootwarden staff, briar wand, hearthbloom) cannot be used, and the six-school icon set needs Tine redone as fire before it is kept. The game has only the wooden staff; wands, foci and tomes are new item lines for Michael. The stormwhistle ties Gaoth to sailing. 'The Weaver's Loom' as an ancient device touches the Church of the Weaver's canon. Michael (review): keep, with Tine redone as fire.

sheet_or_frame: Character proportions: hybrid (the adventurer)
ideas_to_keep: A proportion target for people: heroic-hybrid, about 1.80 m, slightly longer legs and broader shoulders than naturalistic, so silhouettes read at distance and in close combat. The adventurer: brown scale-and-leather armour, a deep teal hooded half-cape, belts of pouches, a sword on the back and a round shield, laced greaves. Silhouette variants with shield, two-handed and cloaked. An in-game scale figure beside the render.
notes: 'Hybrid' implies there were naturalistic and stylised options in other images; which proportions the people rig (32-people.js, 17 bones) follows is a decision for Michael. Applies to the peoples' differences too: canon's short, slight Old Blood and tall, broad Markmen need room either side of 1.80 m. The gold tree emblem on cloak and shield (also OG-087) has no canon meaning yet.

sheet_or_frame: Visual style exploration: four directions
ideas_to_keep: Four style directions: A luminous and painterly, B atmospheric and epic, C seasonal and textured, D mystical and unsettling. Architecture: familiar human buildings against the alien geometry of the Weavers. Creatures: "familiar anatomy with a single impossible element". Vignettes that carry the subtext: a Weaver gate "ancient, purposeful and slightly wrong"; "A watchful moment: not every monster is hunting"; "A quiet detail: the carving of an adventurer, the carvers turned away". Keywords: stylised 3D (not low-poly), readable silhouettes, rich natural colour, simple intentional geometry, atmospheric lighting, subtle unease.
notes: Raises a decision: which of A to D is the game's base look.
